==Problem==
A box contains <imath>10</imath> pounds of a nut mix that is <imath>50</imath> percent peanuts, <imath>20</imath> percent cashews, and <imath>30</imath> percent almonds. A second nut mix contains <imath>20</imath> percent peanuts, <imath>40</imath> percent cashews, and <imath>40</imath> percent almonds.They are all added together in one box resulting in a new nut mix that has <imath>40</imath> percent peanuts. How many pounds of cashews are now in the box? 

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 3.5 \qquad\textbf{(B) } 4 \qquad\textbf{(C) } 4.5 \qquad\textbf{(D) } 5 \qquad\textbf{(E) } 6</imath>

==Solution 1==

We are given that <imath>0.2(10) = 2</imath> pounds of cashews in the first box.

Denote the pounds of nuts in the second nut mix as <imath>x.</imath> 

<cmath>5 + 0.2x = 0.4(10 + x)</cmath>
<cmath>5 + 0.2x = 4 + 0.4x </cmath>
<cmath>5 - 4 = 0.4x - 0.2x </cmath>
<cmath>0.2x = 1</cmath>
<cmath>x = 5</cmath>

Thus, we have <imath>5</imath> pounds of the second mix. 

<cmath>0.4(5) + 2 = 2 + 2 = \boxed{\text{(B) }4}</cmath>

==Solution 2==

Let the number of pounds of nuts in the second nut mixture be <imath>x</imath>. Therefore, we get the equation <imath>0.5 \cdot 10 + 0.2 \cdot x = 0.4(x+10)</imath>. Solving it, we then get <imath>x=5</imath>. Therefore, the amount of cashews in the two bags is <imath>(0.2 \cdot 10) + (0.4
\cdot 5) = 4</imath>, so our answer choice is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)} 4}</imath>.

==Solution 3==

The percent of peanuts in the first mix is <imath>10\%</imath> away from the total percentage of peanuts, and the percent of peanuts in the second mix is <imath>20\%</imath> away from the total percentage. This means the first mix has twice as many nuts as the second mix, so the second mix has <imath>5</imath> pounds. 
<imath>0.20 \cdot 10 + 0.40 \cdot 5 = 4</imath> pounds of cashews. So our answer is, <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}4}</imath>

The weight of the second box of nut mix can be calculated by: (<imath>0.2x + 5) / (10 + x) = 0.4</imath>, where the numerator is equal to the weight of the peanuts, the denominator is equal to the total weight of the boxes, and <imath>x</imath> is equal to the weight of the second box.

Multiplying both sides by <imath>10 + x</imath>, you get <imath>0.2x + 5 = 4 + 0.4x</imath>

Isolating the variable: <imath>0.2x = 1</imath>
<imath>\Rightarrow x = 5</imath>

Calculating the weight of the cashews: <imath>5(0.4) + 10(0.2)</imath>
<imath>\Rightarrow 2 + 2</imath>
<imath>\Rightarrow 4</imath>

The answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 4}</imath>.

==Solution 4==
Note that we can set the information given in the problem into a table shown below:

<cmath>\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
\begin{centering}
\begin{array}{| c | c | c |}
\hline
\text{Peanuts} & \text{Cashews} & \text{Almonds}\\
\hline
5 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
\frac{2}{10}x & \frac{4}{10}x & \frac{4}{10}x\\
\hline
\end{array}
\end{centering}
</cmath>

We are given that the new nut mix will contain <imath>40\%</imath> peanuts. Hence, <imath>5 + \frac{2}{10}x</imath> is <imath>40\%</imath> of the total mix which is <imath>10 + x</imath>. 
Solving the equation <imath>5 + \frac{2}{10}x = \frac{2}{5} \cdot (10 + x)</imath> yields <imath>x=5.</imath> Therefore, the number of cashews in the new mix is equal to <imath>2 + \frac{2}{5} \cdot 5 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}  4}</imath>.

==Solution 5==

Write composition vectors as column vectors (mass fractions multiplied by mass):

Initial mass vector (peanuts, cashews, almonds) for 10 lb:
<cmath>
\mathbf{v}_0 = 10 \begin{pmatrix} 0.50 \\ 0.20 \\ 0.30 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}.
</cmath>
Added mix per unit mass:
<cmath>
\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 0.20 \\ 0.40 \\ 0.40 \end{pmatrix}.
</cmath>
After adding \( x \) lb, total mass vector is
<cmath>
\mathbf{v}(x) = \mathbf{v}_0 + x \mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} + x \begin{pmatrix} 0.2 \\ 0.4 \\ 0.4 \end{pmatrix}.
</cmath>
Peanut fraction requirement:
<cmath>
\frac{\mathbf{e}_1^\top \mathbf{v}(x)}{\mathbf{1}^\top \mathbf{v}(x)} = 0.4,
</cmath>
where \( \mathbf{e}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1, 0, 0 \end{pmatrix}^\top \) and \( \mathbf{1} = \begin{pmatrix} 1, 1, 1 \end{pmatrix}^\top \). This is exactly the same scalar equation,
<cmath>
\frac{5 + 0.2x}{10 + x} = 0.4,
</cmath>
leading to \( x = 5 \) and hence
<cmath>
\mathbf{v}(5) = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} + 5 \begin{pmatrix} 0.2 \\ 0.4 \\ 0.4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}.
</cmath>
Thus cashews \( = 4 \) lb.

==Solution 6: Very easy algebra and straightforward! == 
Set up the ratios for the initial and the additional mixtures. The ratio of Peanuts:Cashews:Almonds (denoted as P:C:A) would initially be <imath>5x:2x:3x</imath> for some factor <imath>x</imath>. Then for the second mixture it would be <imath>2x:4x:4x</imath>. If we add these we get 7x:6x:7x. Now we know that the percentage of peanuts is 40\%. But we also know that the number of pounds of peanuts and almonds is the same. <imath>40\%+40\%=80\%</imath> and so the number of cashews makes up <imath>20\%</imath> of the mixture. If you divide the factor <imath>x</imath> by the whole ratio you get <imath>7:6:7</imath> . These values sum to <imath>20</imath> and <imath>20\%</imath> of <imath>20</imath> is <imath>4</imath>.
